Olivia — thanks, received the redline and the ask. Quick internal triage below; I’ll consolidate proposed language for the Order Form and MSA and send a single-track reply to you + your legal.

High level answers so we can unblock procurement:
- Downtime trigger: Redwood measures availability per region as percentage of successful inference requests over the 30d rolling window. We can offer a dual definition for the Order Form:
  * Continuous outage: a service unavailability window >= 5 consecutive minutes for a single region (counts toward service credit).
  * Cumulative outage: aggregated minutes of unavailability that exceed X% of the monthly runtime (we’ll propose thresholds).
- Evidence formats: we can provide timestamped request logs (CSV), aggregated uptime reports (PDF), and a KB of tracer snapshots in JSON. We retain incident artifacts for 90 days by default and can extend per order form.
- Maintenance notifications: we can commit to a 72-hour standard notice for planned rolling maintenance affecting <10% capacity, and a separate blackout/major change notice for larger operational work.

Action items I’ll take now:
1) Draft redlined language for the Order Form that reflects the above and includes explicit evidence handoff steps.
2) Attach a support matrix (what we can produce automatically vs on-request) — tagging Grace to confirm the content.
3) Send proposed DocuSign-ready Order Form language for Avalon to review.

@Lauren — can you and legal review the proposed language I’ll drop in a follow-up this afternoon?
@Grace — I’ve attached the support matrix we use internally (prelim); feel free to correct any retention/format specifics.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jonas — attaching the support matrix (support-matrix.csv) and adding a few clarifications from an operational standpoint:

- Evidence detail: request logs will include request_id, timestamp (UTC), region, model_id, response_code, latency_ms. Tracer snapshots will be trimmed to 10MB per incident and delivered as JSON bundles.
- Retention: 90 days for incident artifacts in hosted deployments; for Dedicated we can support a 365-day retention addendum (separate charge).
- Calculation: our monitoring uses 1-minute buckets to calculate availability; cumulative outages are summed per calendar month. Continuous outages are detected by circuit-break thresholds (5m default).
- Maintenance notice: 72 hours for standard rolling maintenance, 14 days for major version upgrades that may require capacity changes. We can provide a quarterly maintenance calendar upon request.

Operational caveats for the Order Form: any requirement for forensic-level packet captures or full raw-system dumps will be handled as a professional services engagement. Otherwise, the above artifacts are available on request and we’ll include an automated uptime report for the billing contact.

—Grace
Grace O’Connor
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia / Marco — thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Below is the consolidated language we propose for insertion into the Order Form and the MSA exhibit (redline-ready). I’ve tried to keep it operationally prescriptive so your legal and procurement can accept it without another round. If this looks right to Avalon legal, I’ll package it into DocuSign and include the small retention addendum as an optional checkbox on the order form.

Proposed Order Form language (excerpt):
1) Availability Measurement and Downtime Triggers
   a) Availability will be measured per-region using 1-minute monitoring buckets and reported as the percentage of successful inference requests over each 30-day rolling period.
   b) Continuous outage: any uninterrupted period of unavailability lasting five (5) consecutive minutes or longer in a single region; such continuous outages will be counted against the Availability calculation.
   c) Cumulative outage: the aggregation of unavailability minutes during the calendar month. If cumulative outage exceeds the thresholds set forth in the Service Credits table, Service Credits will apply.

2) Evidence and Artifact Delivery
   a) On request, Redwood will provide: timestamped request logs (CSV), aggregated uptime reports (PDF), and tracer snapshots (JSON) related to the impacted timeframe.
   b) Redwood will deliver initial evidence within ten (10) business days of a validated incident report; final artifact package will be provided within thirty (30) calendar days unless otherwise agreed.
   c) Incident artifacts will be retained for ninety (90) days in hosted deployments unless an extended retention addendum is selected.

3) Maintenance Notifications
   a) Planned rolling maintenance impacting less than ten percent (10%) of a customer’s capacity: Redwood will provide at least seventy-two (72) hours’ advance notice.
   b) Major infrastructure or version upgrades that may change capacity or require coordinated cutover: Redwood will provide at least fourteen (14) calendar days’ advance notice and a draft cutover plan.

4) Evidence exclusions and professional services
   a) Forensic-level artifacts (e.g., full packet capture or host-level forensic images) are out-of-scope and may be provided under a separate professional services statement of work.

Next steps:
- If Avalon legal is ok with the above, confirm and we’ll follow with a DocuSign package: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC123
- If you want the 365-day retention for hosted artifacts, we’ll add the retention addendum (chargeable) on the order form — let us know.

Olivia — let me know if you want a short call to walk through the proposed language. Otherwise we’ll await your legal’s confirmation and will prepare the DocuSign.

Best,
Jonas Weber
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
